content.title: About
content.content: Sauerkraut is a fermented product made from fresh white cabbage, salt, and sometimes spices. During fermentation, lactic‑acid bacteria convert the cabbage sugars into lactic acid, giving it a characteristic sour taste and extending its shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sauerkraut is a traditional dish in many Eastern and Central European countries.
Fermentation creates probiotic cultures that are beneficial for gut health.
The acidic environment helps preserve vitamin C, which is usually lost during cooking.
In Russia, sauerkraut is commonly used in soups like shchi and borscht, as well as a side dish.
The most famous variety is German sauerkraut, often flavored with caraway seeds and apples.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Fermentation produces live Lactobacillus bacteria that support a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Sauerkraut retains a high level of vitamin C, which helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Rich in dietary fiber, it aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: One cup of sauerkraut contains about 20 calories, making it a great choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides potassium, magnesium, and iron, important for heart function and blood formation.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Sauerkraut often contains a lot of salt, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial Fermentation
items.content: Improper storage can lead to growth of harmful bacteria and spoilage.

items.title: Gas and Bloating
items.content: For some individuals, fermentation may cause increased gas and abdominal discomfort.

items.title: Cabbage Allergy
items.content: Rarely, an allergic reaction to cabbage or its fermented forms can occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauerkraut can be eaten on its own as a snack, added to soups, stews, salads, sandwiches, or used as a side dish for meat and fish. It is often rinsed before serving to reduce excess salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sauerkraut in the refrigerator in an airtight container. When kept properly, it stays fresh for 2–3 weeks. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
